name: British Parliamentary Debate
summary: Four teams of two in one room, two on each side, debate a motion after fifteen minutes of preparation, and the judges rank the teams first to fourth.
who: Mostly university students; it is the format of the World Universities Debating Championship (WUDC). Many high schools and clubs use it too, often with five-minute speeches.
resolution: An impromptu motion for each round, announced fifteen minutes before the debate.

speeches.name: Prime Minister
speeches.job: Define the motion and give the government's first arguments.

speeches.name: Leader of the Opposition
speeches.job: Respond to the definition and case and give the opposition's first arguments.

speeches.name: Deputy Prime Minister
speeches.job: Rebuild, rebut, and add to the opening government case.

speeches.name: Deputy Leader of the Opposition
speeches.job: Rebuild, rebut, and add to the opening opposition case.

speeches.name: Member for the Government
speeches.job: Bring a new line of argument (the "extension") that agrees with the opening government but goes further.

speeches.name: Government Whip
speeches.job: Sum up the debate for the government, with emphasis on why the closing government's extension matters. No new arguments.

speeches.name: Opposition Whip
speeches.job: Sum up the debate for the opposition. No new arguments.

prep.note: Fifteen minutes of preparation after the motion is announced, with each team preparing on its own. University championships allow printed materials but not electronic devices during prep; school and club tournaments set their own rules.

poi.note: Members of the other bench may offer points of information during any speech except in its first and last minute. A point lasts up to about 15 seconds, and the speaker may accept or decline.

rewards: Quick thinking: the motion is new every round
Arguments that are well explained, not just asserted
For closing teams, a new and important extension
Engaging with the whole room, including through points of information
start: Learn the four positions and what each speaker's job is.
Practice fifteen-minute preparation with a partner and a sheet of paper.
Read old motions from university tournaments and talk through both sides.
Watch a WUDC final online and note how the closing teams find new ground.
varies: Speech length: seven minutes at university level; five minutes is common in schools.
Materials during preparation and the round depend on the tournament.
Some leagues give first-time speakers protection from points of information.

p: The government bench supports the motion and the opposition bench opposes it, but each of the four teams competes against all three others, including the team on its own side. The judges rank the teams first to fourth (in the usual scoring, 3, 2, 1 and 0 points).
A closing team can't simply repeat its opening team; it must add something new and important (an **extension**). The whips then sum up the whole debate for their bench.

sources.title: WUDC Debating & Judging Manual (Ottawa WUDC 2027 edition), the authoritative rules
Debating Tutorial Handouts: British Parliamentary (C. Flynn)

topicShort: A new impromptu motion each round
